cells.tense: You are holding what the change left behind, and you are doing it in plain sight.
cells.ask: Hand one person something you have been keeping for them, and name what it cost you to hold it. No ledger. Just the item and the cost.
cells.core: Something ended, and what came out of it is still here with you — kept, not buried. You can sit with another person and feel what they feel without vanishing into it. Right now that line holds. Give and take move in an easy rhythm: you say what you need, you hear what they need, and neither side is tallying.\n\nYou are not guarding the thing, and you are not disappearing into the person you kept it for. You are simply in the room with what you saved, and with them. What keeps this working is that you keep passing it along. Holding it was only ever the first half of the motion. Handing it over is the part that finishes it.
cells.sheetLine: You hold it and stay reachable at the same time.

cells.place: where two people feel along the same line without becoming one

cells.tense: You are bracing for a conversation that has not happened, guarding a door nobody has knocked on yet.
cells.ask: Let one conversation you have already rehearsed stay unhad today. If it comes, answer with what is actually in the room, not the version you prepared.
cells.core: Steady, this reads a person accurately and still knows where you end. You feel what they feel, you stay yourself, and you let things arrive at their own pace instead of hauling them forward by the collar.\n\nInstead you are holding the reaction before anyone has reacted. A word gets said and you are three steps ahead, arranging the thing so it cannot break. The protecting is real work, and all of it is happening ahead of any threat. What you are preserving may not need this much. The other person cannot reach the part of you that is actually here, because most of you is standing in a room that has not arrived. Your care is genuine. Your timing is early.

cells.tense: You left the doorway behind you and you are still standing in it, deciding whether to come in.
cells.ask: Say one true thing about what you are keeping to one person, without giving it away, fixing it, or asking them to carry it.
cells.core: Steady, this moves from what you actually feel. Warmth becomes a hand reached out instead of a thing kept in a case. You step toward the person rather than watching from the edge, and the feeling underneath gives the step its direction.\n\nInstead, something got built and something got saved, and you have not stepped into the room it belongs to. You can feel the person nearby, but you are outside the exchange, watching it go on without you. Keeping it safe has become the place you live. The feeling is there; moving from it is not. What is missing isn't the willingness to feel. It's the willingness to let the feeling point somewhere and then go there yourself.

cells.tense: You are already setting how the room holds what it has, and you describe that as the situation being what it is.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you have been calling 'just how it is,' and say whose keeping-it-that-way it actually is. Out loud, once, to no one in particular.
cells.core: Steady, the structure you make serves the people inside it. Things are clear, people relax around you, and what you set up holds them without needing a speech to explain it. Your version of this works, and it is close.\n\nInstead, you are the one setting the shape of this. The calm people feel near you comes from choices you are making, not from circumstances arranging themselves. You say it is timing, it is the situation, it is the other person needing something. You are already doing the thing. You just are not saying it is yours. Saying it once will not make it heavier. It will make it usable by the people it is holding.

attempts.check: The draft claims a specific relational history — that the balanced state means fairness flows and both people are honored — but the record cannot know who is in the room or what it costs. A reader could reasonably say 'you're describing a calm I don't have; the fairness I manage is exhausting, not flowing.' The ask survives being wrong: it can be done by someone who is exhausted, hoarding, or over-functioning, because it is still an act of exchange, not a feeling. The sentence that would serve me is 'peaceful stability through form' — that phrase is the record's, not the person's, and I will not put it on glass.
